\section{Higgs boson} The following is a link to a \PMlinkexternal{simplified demonstration using $Mathematica^{TM}$ for the generation of the Higgs boson}{http://demonstrations.wolfram.com/TheHiggsParticle/}, a (hypothetical) fundamental, neutral scalar particle $H^0$ which is supposed to be detected `soon' by one of the two Tevatron, particle accellerators presently in operation. One can have a free download of this demonstration and play the oversimplified simulation as a color animation with the $Mathematica^{TM}$ Player (which is also a free download that does not save however).
According to the current Standard Model theory, various particles are supposed to acquire mass only via their interactions with the neutral scallar Higgs boson, $H^0$. (A Nobel prize has already been predicted for such a hypothetical discovery that would close the gap between the current Standard Model theory and experimental, high energy physics.)
